items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Al Cohn, I gave him the Duke Ellington things, and Manny Albam the Basie things.

ctx.x: That was just a fluke. It was the biggest fluke. I recorded a band in New York in 1956 or something like that and I was sick because it wasn’t good — not to me, it wasn’t good. I used the same rhythm section that was with my little group. I always try to use the guys who travel with me and kill themselves on the road, to give them a good job. If I did a T.V. show, I was steadily using a quartet, three of the guys from the house band, I want my guys on there. I always tried to push them on there. So I put them on…

idea was I was going to hire six different arrangers and pay tribute to six different band leaders, like Duke Ellington, Lionel Hampton, Count Basie, Tommy Dorsey, Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw. And I was going to take something out of each arrangement, like Artie Shaw’s clarinet chorus on “Stardust” just the first 16 bars, and somewhere would sneak it in the arrangement, or part of Ben Webster’s chorus on “Cottontail,” whatever, you know. And I hired the arrangers that I thought would write for those guys. I put…
But they want you in the studio.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But if Johnny Mandel was alive or Al Cohn or Manny Albam, these great arrangers, they would tell you they learned arranging from what Tiny was doing.

ctx.x: Everybody in the world has one. So, and you could relate to all, and all kids who play in the streets could relate to my stories, you know. So and I was lucky to have a great childhood. I grew up with Tiny Kahn, see Tiny Kahn is when I was from 6 years old until I went in the Army at 19 or 18, until I got with Woody Herman’s band really. We were together day and night. And if you can, people who know these names can imagine what we looked like at 15 years old, we looked like Peter Lorre and Sydney Greenstreet…
